reasons: Lake identity names State v. Wint, court N.J. 2018, date decided 2018-12-12, and docket A-28/29 September Term 2017; 079660.
Lake citations list official citation 236 N.J. 174 and parallel citation 198 A.3d 963; the content citation matches exactly.
The opinion states that Wint remained in continuous pre-indictment custody for six months and therefore no break in custody occurred under Shatzer.
The opinion states the Edwards/Shatzer exceptions as counsel provided, defendant initiated communication, or break in custody, and says none applied.
The opinion states repeated Miranda warnings did not cure the Edwards violation and that Edwards required suppression of the incriminating statement.
The case centrally concerns Miranda warnings, invocation of counsel, later waiver, and the Edwards rule after invocation.
The opinion describes Wint receiving Miranda warnings, invoking counsel twice, later waiving after renewed warnings, and the court holding the later waiver ineffective under Edwards.
residual_risks: No separate home-page rubric for the label 'Key' is disclosed, but the opinion text supports this as a central Miranda waiver/invocation authority.
